GABA modulates the function of bushy cells in the auditory pathway by converting them from a simple relay into a coincidence-detector.
the neuromodulator GABA converts a BC relay cell into a coincidence detector.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how GABA affects the processing of auditory information by the brainstem.
understanding the functional impact of neuromodulation by γ-amin-butyric acid (GABA), which is a common feature at relay cells in sensory pathways.
the role of neuromodulators in the processing of auditory information by the brain stem auditory system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuromodulatory action of GABA on a relay cell converts it into a coincidence detector, and thus into a more efficient information processing element.
GABA converts a BC into a coincidence detector.
GABA converts the function of BC relay cells from that of a simple integrator of single AN inputs to that of a coincidence detector of AN input pairs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GABA converts a BC from a simple relay to a coincidence detector.
GABA converts a single relay neuron into a coincidence detector.
GABA converts the relay function of BCs to a coincidence detector, and thereby could contribute to the formation of auditory objects.

GABA can convert a relay into a coincident detector.
